title: MV Input Spam when Holding a Button (Octobattle)

posts.author: LunarMelodia
posts.body:
Hi all,
Firstly I definitely posted this the wrong place earlier and I don't know how to delete it...
I'm really sorry about that and I hope someone can point me towards how I can do that so there isn't a duplicate post!
So, recently got back into RPG Making, and installed Yanfly's GamepadConfig plugin.
My issue is what when I hold any button down, it spams the input of that button infinitely until I let it go. As a result I can zoom through menus at lightspeed and very easily misclick options.
But the
real
problem comes from the fact that I'm using Olivia's Octobattle system. I've got Page Up / Down set to the Left and Right trigger on my gamepad, but when I press either trigger even a tiny bit to increase my Boost level, it maxes it out all the way as if I'd pressed it like 5 times.
This is obviously for the same reason as above, the input spam when holding a button down.
How do I prevent this input spam in all cases?
Thanks in advance for the help!
Edit:
Here are video examples I made later in the thread for those newly joining

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
I don't have a gamepad to test with myself, but here are some ideas:
If the issue only occurs with a gamepad, do you happen to have any other gamepads (make/model) that you can test with, to see if the problem persists? E.g. I believe Xbox controllers are widely supported on modern PCs. Less common gamepads, particularly older models, are less likely to be correctly supported.
Do you see the same kind of problem in a new project, with no plugins? E.g. a plugin may have mistakenly used an
isPressed
check instead of
isRepeated
. If it only occurs with plugins enabled, that suggests it's a plugin issue.
Do you see the same problem in other games?
If it only seems to occur in RPG Maker MV/Z games (which, to be clear, are browser-based regardless of deploy target), it may be related to the way their core scripts, and/or the plugins used, process those inputs.
If it occurs in HTML/browser games in general, the problem may be that your gamepad doesn't work nicely with the browser's Gamepad API. There might be a general solution via 3rd-party software, or specific, per-game solutions.
If it occurs in non-HTML games too, it may be a quirk of your gamepad, or some background software you're using that intercepts/interprets the gamepad input signals.

So it happens with keyboard
or
gamepad input, even with no plugins enabled? If so, that's very important information~
As stated earlier, plugins are responsible for handling their own input, so it may also be a problem with Olivia's Octobattle plugin. Since that plugin is paid, though (and probably obfuscated) you're unlikely to find anyone to help with it, other than its author.
Like others have mentioned, the problem sounds like core behaviour:
isRepeated
is false until the button is long-pressed (24 frames), then is true every "repeat interval" (6 frames) after that. MZ implements a
_canRepeat
flag on selectable windows to control stuff like this, toggling between
isRepeated
and
isTriggered
for relevant checks, but MV doesn't. Your game appears to be running at 60 fps according to the F2 widget, so 24 frames should last 24/60 = 0.4 seconds. It's possible you are holding the button slightly longer than that, per press.
Did you try the code
@utunnels
provided in earlier posts (
#14
,
#16
) to change the repeat times? I.e. as a plugin:
JavaScript:
// A button is long-pressed after being held for 10000 frames.
Input.keyRepeatWait = 10000;   // default 24
// The button repeat check will be true every 60 frames after that.
Input.keyRepeatInterval = 60;  // default 6
As before, test first in a new project, else other plugins may interfere. Alternatively:
JavaScript:
// Override!
Input.isRepeated = function() {
  this.isTriggered.apply(this, arguments);
};
This basically makes all
isRepeated
checks act as
isTriggered
: true iff the button was not pressed on the previous frame, but is pressed right now. Either solution will be sub-optimal in various cases, but if they solve your primary problem of "zooming through menus etc" then that's a promising start!
You could also try typing this into the console window, then press Enter:
process.versions.nw
This reports the version of NWJS (runtime app) your game is running on. E.g. I see this:
If you're using a different version, e.g. because you manually upgraded it at some point, that may be noteworthy.
If you have, at any point, modified your project's core scripts (or, worse, the core scripts in your RMMV install folder, under NewData) you could restore them to defaults (e.g. by reinstalling your editor, or using Steam's "verify file integrity" feature) then make a new project and retry the tests in that clean project.
At the end of the day, it's not feasible for us to suggest a fix if we can't understand or even replicate the problem on our end.

Oh. Have you tried to reproduce that behaviour with a minimal setup, i.e. only Octobattle plugins in their recommended load order? I advise testing in a new project, to be sure nothing else is interfering.
You could double-check that all plugins you're using are up-to-date. Also, Yanfly's stuff has a recommended load order, and e.g. Olivia's Boost Point System states that it is compatible with a number of Yanfly's plugins if loaded after them (i.e. Boost Point System should appear somewhere below the Yanfly stuff in your Plugin Manager list). If you're not sure about load order, you could post screenshot(s) of your Plugin Manager for someone here to check.
Based on screenshots, it looks like the Boost Point System plugin has a plugin parameter to toggle that feature: "Use L and R buttons". So I think you could avoid the problem if you're willing to force players to use the actor commands to (de)allocate boost points.
Since Olivia's terms of use explicitly allow editing the code (but, obviously, not sharing it) you could try Ctrl+F ->
Input.isPressed
. If you find it, you could make a copy of the plugin (as a backup), then try replacing
Input.isPressed
with either
Input.isTriggered
or
Input.isRepeated
, to see if that helps.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
There is no way to contact her.
Doesn't really feel good to pay for a product that offers no support huh
Unfortunately this is not the first (nor will it be the last) time something like this has happened.
There was a memory leak in one of her other plugins that we were able to patch out, mostly by luck due to her obfuscating the code. I think that's what makes the commercial part of it even worse is not only does she not offer support for her product any more, she also prevents people from supporting it themselves.
Great gal, that Olivia. You can also add Aries to that list of super great people too.

posts.author: LunarMelodia
posts.body:
Hi everyone, it's been a little while and I never ended up fixing this issue.
So this is a PSA to anyone who is considering using Olivia's Octobattle plugin.
Don't.
I'm either going to redesign my entire combat system from the ground up or commission someone to make their own version of an Octobattle style plugin.
Thanks to everyone that tried to help me.
